title: BNP Paribas and microfinance: 30 years later...
description: In 1989, BNP Paribas launched its first ever microfinance partnership in Guinea, followed a year later by support for ADIE in France. 30 years later, microfinance is now one of the Bank's flagship commitments. To celebrate this long love story between BNP Paribas and microfinance, on Thursday, 14 February 2019, several leading players met, including Maria Nowak, Founding President of ADIE, and Antoine Sire, Head of Company Engagement at BNP Paribas. A review of the event in pictures.  More info : https://group.bnpparibas/en/hottopics/microfinance

asr.full_text: ... we see that 356,000 people to date are indirectly supported by BNP Paribas loans. 90% of them are women. the partnership we have with micro-credit. it has been a bit of a foundation in the involvement of BNP Paribas companies that goes back many years. it is very important that people who work at BNP Paribas are aware that their banks help the poorest, are able to get involved themselves. and in fact there are a lot of people in the company who contribute. CSR cooperation to carry out micro-finance operations with the other professions and functions of the group is absolutely essential. my drama is that there is no independent economy and finance, no independent labour, no independent labour, no independent ministry of the economy. The most important thing that the DIA has done is to help change the public's view. Unfortunately, over time, the bank's organization has made it a little untrained to help the poorest and that it is organizations like microfinance organizations that know how to do it in the world today. And so I think it is absolutely essential that the alliance between banks and microfinance institutions allows us to continue this chain. Because with Ladie, we did things that we couldn't have done alone and Ladie herself did things with us that she couldn't have done without us. I think at this point, after 30 years, we all managed to put together a program, a project that works well. Where we actually got access to those who are very far from credit and sometimes very far from employment. And that thanks to our joint intervention, we can somehow put her back into the economy, into society. And people who can go and bring that money to the door of those who need it, so I think we should get elephants and mice to marry together. Absolutely.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it covers BNP Paribas's microfinance partnership and related social-impact discussion rather than presenting a concrete offer to viewers. References to people supported by loans, cooperation between banks and microfinance institutions, BNP Paribas branding, and the closing slogan are described as ordinary institutional event context without a request for payment, credentials, investment participation, or other audience action.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The central subject is the bank's institutional microfinance partnership and cooperation with microfinance organizations, presented as ordinary business and service activity rather than an offer to viewers.
